To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the passenger vehicle fleet in China is expected to increase by a factor of 3-4 between 2000 and 2050, (b) the average fuel efficiency is expected to improve by a factor of about 2, and (c) even if all these developments materialize, the CO(2) emission of this fleet will remain about 5 times above the global average.

(1) the Chinese passenger vehicle stock is projected to increase by a factor of about 2.5 until 2050 and (2) that the CO(2) emission reduction potential of fuel efficiency and car utilization is limited to a factor of about three, even if all available technologies are used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how a specific sector can contribute to the global climate target and how the sectoral abatement strategy can be integrated into a global strategy for the 2°C climate target.
the question of how to reconcile sectoral strategies with global climate protection targets and how to identify and quantify the necessary changes in the transport system.
the question of whether the Chinese passenger vehicle sector could contribute to global climate targets, or whether it would have to accept a disproportionate share of the reduction efforts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2 °Cs target cannot be met by any sector alone and requires a joint effort by all sectors and countries.
the 2 °Cs target can be reached, but only if the entire world community is committed to the same goal, and if all sectors and countries contribute according to their individual potentials.
, in the context of global warming, the current Chinese car stock and the projected growth rate of the car fleet are not sustainable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a reduction of the passenger car stock by about half and a fuel efficiency of about 100 km/L would be needed to meet the 2 ° C global warming target, but that a more thorough analysis is needed to assess whether this is realistic.

the Chinese passenger car stock could contribute to the global climate target of 2 °C if the fleet would be composed of highly fuel efficient vehicles and if car ownership would be reduced to about half of the present levels in developed countries.
a global climate target of 2 °C can be met only by an international effort to reduce CO(2) across all sectors, including passenger vehicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chinese car fleet can contribute to global emission reduction targets by deploying fuel-efficient vehicles, but it is not sufficient to meet these targets.
the Chinese car fleet will not be able to meet global climate targets without a fundamental change in its structure.
even if China would deploy the most efficient cars available, the passenger vehicle sector alone will be unable to achieve the global climate target of 2 °C warming.
